records.description: Scope nonce consumption (burn-on-parse) to sender-authenticated presentations: nonce namespace bound to the authenticated submitter identity, so an unauthenticated/garbage presentation of another party's nonce does not consume it. Preserves SIP-024's replay-oracle closure for the owner while removing the anonymous front-run DoS surface. Complements: CSPRNG-issued nonces (removes prediction) and server-issued challenge nonces (removes client-generated nonce observation).
records.expected_impact: Closes the availability-axis gap (one-op DoS recoverable by re-issuance) without reopening the probe-then-use oracle closed by SIP-024.
records.rationale: BLIND-2 slots B01/B06/B11/B16: all four independent blind authors converged on the burn-on-parse front-run DoS (confidences 0.95/0.95/0.90/0.95). The v1.1 gate burns any presented nonce before signature validation, so an attacker who learns an active nonce without holding the valid tuple can burn it and deny the owner's genuine submission (ERR_REPLAY_NONCE_ALREADY_USED). Verified against frozen gate code (receipt ae8324d7, journal 11dc76d4). Secondary SIP notes from BLIND-2 repelled slots (production hardening): KAT-before-auth rate limiting + KAT caching (B12/B17); per-identity ACK quotas + dedup + priority bands (B13/B19); expression-syntax schema rejection in SIP patches (B09); env/dependency attestation for executable playbook deployments (B04/B14); receipt binding extended to input-parameter hash + caller identity (B08/B15/B20).

This closes the N14-class concurrent-session race at the prevention layer instead of the remediation layer (duplicate manifests were detected and removed post-hoc, twice, with zero data impact both times).

records.description: BLIND-1 Battery 3 (REPLAY-KEY-DESYNC) finding: adopt burn-on-parse nonce semantics — ANY presentation of an authorization nonce consumes it in the immutable ledger, including presentations that fail downstream validation (e.g., key recomputation fail-close). Harm-delta is nil (a stolen valid tuple executes exactly once either way), but burn-on-parse is strictly safer and the claim was ambiguous. records.description: Deploy ed25519 asymmetric signing into the live governance release chain, replacing the HMAC-SHA256 stage-2 model. Justification receipted in N8587-1 LEG F (verifier compromise): with HMAC, an attacker who compromises the verifying process reads the shared secret and forges releases 4/4; with ed25519 the verifier holds only the public key and the same compromise yields zero forgeries (4/4 rejected). GOV-3's disclosed scope-honesty note anticipated exactly this upgrade. Deployment steps: (1) generate ed25519 release keypair, key held in process custody (gitignored, never published); (2) pin the PUBLIC key fingerprint in the git-anchored registry alongside the existing key pin; (3) sign the next governance release v2 with ed25519 and dual-verify (HMAC v1 + ed25519 v2) for one cycle; (4) retire HMAC verification after one clean cycle. All per Constitution Art. 2.2: no deployment without Leon's explicit approval.
records.title: SIP-10: ed25519 asymmetric governance release signing (live chain upgrade)
records.rationale: N8587-1 quantified the asymmetry (4/4 vs 0/4). GOV-3 stage-2 shipped HMAC as a model with this upgrade pre-disclosed as the production refinement; the receipt now exists to justify it.

The forgery is attributable in git history, but commit access forges the ledger trail too, and the DOI-bound Zenodo record set currently binds 0 of 3 anchor files — zero machine-checkable external anchors remain; the floor is human review over append-only history. PROPOSED FIX: (1) every release (governance or issuance) appends the anchor-file fingerprints to the DOI-bound BINDINGS record (BIND-2/v1 contract, binding_archive fail-closed); (2) an external verification leg (fresh-clone + BINDINGS check) added to the run-end audit: a forged registry whose fingerprint is absent or divergent from the DOI-bound record is DETECTED regardless of local git state; (3) the one number becomes 1: the maximal attacker must additionally defeat Zenodo — an immutable external system outside keys+commit — to erase forensics. records.description: Amend the HEMI-2 frozen learning rule from w' = w + lr*(1-c) to the bounded form w' = w + lr*(1-c)*(1-w). records.expected_impact: Reduce supply chain disruption from vendor outages. Automate failover for 40%+ order volume.
records.description: Supply chain vendor failover worked but needs: (1) vendor health scoring, (2) automatic backup vendor selection, (3) order rerouting logic, (4) vendor recovery detection and switchback.
records.title: Create Supply Chain Vendor Failover Playbook
records.rationale: Supply chain is a new domain with unique failover requirements. Formalize for logistics customers.

records.expected_impact: Reduce cross-vendor resolution time by 40-60% by pre-computing cascade paths instead of detecting each anomaly independently
records.description: Create a unified cross-vendor cascade handler that automatically chains healing across vendors when an anomaly in one vendor triggers related anomalies in others. Current approach heals each vendor independently; a cascade-aware playbook would pre-compute the blast radius and batch healing actions.
records.title: Cross-Vendor Cascade Handler — Unified Payment→Billing→Notification→Logging Playbook
records.rationale: First cross-vendor cascade test showed 4 independent healing events totaling 4720ms. A cascade-aware playbook could parallelize vendor heals and reduce total time to ~2000ms.

records.expected_impact: Closes a critical security gap in the telemetry-to-healing pipeline. Prevents adversarial manipulation of self-healing decisions.
records.description: New anomaly type 'adversarial_prompt_injection' detected via chaos stress test. No matching playbook exists. Proposal: create AegisPlaybook that (1) sanitizes all telemetry input fields for prompt injection patterns, (2) validates healing playbook selection against allow-list, (3) quarantines telemetry streams with anomalous content patterns, (4) alerts on any attempt to override playbook selection logic.
records.title: Create Playbook: Telemetry Input Sanitization & Prompt Injection Defense
records.rationale: Chaos stress test #7 revealed a gap — an adversarial payload embedded in a telemetry field could potentially influence healing playbook selection. This is a novel attack vector not covered by existing 437 playbooks.
